title: Indefinite leave to remain if you have a Skilled Worker, Health and Care Worker, T2 or Tier 2 visa: Time in the UK - GOV.UK

content.p: You must have lived in the UK for 5 years before you can apply for indefinite leave to remain.
There are rules for what counts towards the 5 years if you have:

content.li: been a partner or child (a ‘dependant) on a visa

content.h2: If you’ve spent time outside the UK

content.p: You must have spent no more than 180 days outside the UK in any 12 months.
If you think you’re affected by this rule, the Home Office has guidance about how to calculate your time in the UK (‘continuous residence’).

content.h2: If you’ve been a partner or child (a ‘dependant’) on a visa

content.p: In the 5 years you’ve lived in the UK, you cannot include any time you’ve spent in the UK as a partner or child (a ‘dependant’) on a visa.

content.h2: If you’ve had more than one visa

content.p: In the 5 years you’ve lived in the UK, you can include time you’ve had on any combination of the following visas:

content.li: any Tier 1 visa - except Tier 1 (Graduate Entrepreneur)
Skilled Worker, Health and Care Worker or Tier 2 (General)
T2 Minister of Religion or Tier 2 (Minister of Religion)
International Sportsperson, T2 Sportsperson or Tier 2 (Sportsperson)
